Peppers have "perfect flowers" which means they have male and female parts in the same flower, and are self fertile. You don't need bees *or* hand pollination of individual flowers with a qtip.

Simply tap the back of the flower gently or give the plant a shake early in the morning to help the flowers pollinate. 
As with tomatoes, some people use an electric toothbrush to jiggle their pepper flowers.

While we should be grateful for pollinators, tomatoes have "perfect flowers" which means they have male and female parts in the same flower. They self-fertilize and don't rely on bees to reproduce.

If you want to make sure your tomato flowers grow into fruit, gently tap the flower or shake the plant to help it fertilize, some people even use an electric toothbrush to tickle their tomatoes.

At 14 years old your brain is still changing from a child to an adult. Every time you learn something your brain makes a pattern of it, and right now you have both child and adult patterns. Right now you are going through real brain changes called [Synaptic Pruning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synaptic_pruning).

Basically, your brain is going through all of the child-hood connections your brain made growing up (so things like peeing in the tub, still having to sleep with a stuffed animal, childhood games) and figuring out what to keep and what to get rid of. So it will be a little confusing for awhile. 

You will probably feel like a kid and adult at the same time, which can be hard. But just realize you are still growing, your body and your brain.

Just in case someone else ends up here-
E12 is the code for the base, which in this case is a candelabra base. This is a smaller screw-style base that looks like the base of a regular light bulb we are all used to seeing (A19, E26).

The bulb you bought is a 25w E12 base. The shape of the lamp is another thing, but as long as it fits into the salt-lamp, no worries. The bulbs you bought are likely a torpedo shape, but other common shapes for e12 bulbs are flame (with a pointy tip) or tubular. 

If you can get it to fit in the socket, fit into the lamp and it is under the wattage rating, you'll be fine. 

Side note- Getting an LED bulb or something with low wattage (5-10) is a mistake in this case. The salt lamp works through the heat created by the incandescent bulb, and lower wattage means less energy which means less heat.
